title: Migration starts with a dependency map
points: Inventory applications, servers, databases, owners, network flows and data gravity. Map dependencies before sequencing cutover; distinguish discovery evidence from assumptions.
layout: thin glass architecture teaching pane with glossy symbols

title: Assess the portfolio before selecting a path
points: Classify business criticality, technical fit, data sensitivity, downtime, licensing and operating cost; group workloads by modernization value and migration complexity.
layout: thin glass architecture teaching pane with glossy symbols

title: Migration waves follow dependency order
points: Group tightly coupled components into waves. Establish landing zone, network, identity and observability first; pilot low-risk workloads, then move dependent services together.
layout: thin glass architecture teaching pane with glossy symbols

title: Choose a migration strategy by constraint
points: Compare retain, retire, relocate, rehost, replatform, repurchase, refactor. Each option trades speed, change effort and long-term operating model; choose per application.
layout: thin glass architecture teaching pane with glossy symbols

title: The migration factory has repeatable gates
points: Assess -> mobilize -> replicate/build -> test -> cut over -> stabilize. Each wave has owner, acceptance criteria, fallback and measured outcomes.
layout: thin glass architecture teaching pane with glossy symbols

title: Rehost a server with AWS Transform MGN
points: Agent-based continuous replication from source server to staging area, launch test instance, validate application and network, then cut over to EC2. Use current AWS Transform MGN naming.
layout: thin glass architecture teaching pane with glossy symbols

title: Test launch is not cutover
points: Compare test launch and cutover launch in MGN. Check instance sizing, IAM, security groups, DNS, data freshness and rollback plan before directing production traffic.
layout: thin glass architecture teaching pane with glossy symbols

title: AWS Transform modernizes at portfolio scale
points: Use AWS Transform for assessed modernization workflows such as VMware or mainframe/application transformation where supported; human review of generated plans and validation remains essential.
layout: thin glass architecture teaching pane with glossy symbols

title: Select the right data transfer path
points: DataSync transfers files/objects with validation and scheduling; Storage Gateway bridges hybrid storage; Transfer Family provides managed SFTP/FTPS/FTP endpoints. Choose by source protocol and operating requirement.
layout: thin glass architecture teaching pane with glossy symbols

title: Database migration has two separate changes
points: DMS migrates and replicates data; AWS SCT or schema conversion addresses heterogeneous schema and code. Same-engine versus heterogeneous paths need different compatibility work.
layout: thin glass architecture teaching pane with glossy symbols

title: DMS full load plus CDC
points: Full load copies baseline, change data capture keeps target near source, validation compares results, then freeze writes and cut over. Monitor lag, task errors and unsupported objects.
layout: thin glass architecture teaching pane with glossy symbols

title: Large data has a physics problem
points: Compare online transfer time against available bandwidth, change rate and cutover window; offline Snow Family/data transfer options may suit bulk import. Encrypt, validate, and plan delta synchronization.
layout: thin glass architecture teaching pane with glossy symbols

title: Replatform to managed data services
points: Move compatible database to RDS or Aurora, files to S3/EFS, and app runtime to ECS or Lambda. Preserve schema, connection behavior, IAM and recovery semantics.
layout: thin glass architecture teaching pane with glossy symbols

title: Modernization is incremental
points: Strangler pattern routes one capability at a time from legacy monolith to new service. API façade, event integration and shared-data boundary are explicit; avoid a risky big-bang rewrite.
layout: thin glass architecture teaching pane with glossy symbols

title: Decompose by business capability
points: Find bounded contexts, data ownership and synchronous call hotspots. Extract one capability with measurable contract, observability and rollback before further decomposition.
layout: thin glass architecture teaching pane with glossy symbols

title: Mainframe and legacy modernization
points: Assess transaction interfaces, batch jobs, data encoding, dependency mapping and compliance. Choose rehost/replatform/refactor based on functionality and operational constraints.
layout: thin glass architecture teaching pane with glossy symbols

title: Integrate the legacy edge safely
points: API Gateway or ALB façade, Lambda adapters, Amazon MQ for existing messaging protocols, and events for decoupling. Control auth, retries, idempotency and ordering at boundaries.
layout: thin glass architecture teaching pane with glossy symbols

title: Cutover is a rehearsed transaction
points: Pre-cutover validation, data sync and freeze, DNS/traffic switch, smoke tests, ownership handoff, and rollback trigger. TTL alone does not guarantee instant client change.
layout: thin glass architecture teaching pane with glossy symbols

title: Walkthrough: migrate a three-tier application
points: Discover web/app/database dependencies, choose rehost app plus managed database, replicate and test, cut over with health verification, then decommission old endpoints after stabilization.
layout: thin glass architecture teaching pane with glossy symbols

title: Walkthrough: database migration with minimal downtime
points: Assess schema and compatibility, convert if heterogeneous, run DMS full load+CDC, verify lag and data, pause writes, cut over connection string, monitor and retain rollback window.
layout: thin glass architecture teaching pane with glossy symbols

title: Modernize after the first landing
points: After rehost, collect performance and cost data; rightsize, harden, add managed operations, then extract high-value capabilities. Migration completion and modernization completion are distinct.
layout: thin glass architecture teaching pane with glossy symbols

title: Migration security is end to end
points: Map source/target identity, encryption in transit and at rest, secrets, private routes, least privilege, audit logs and data residency. Test restore and access paths in target.
layout: thin glass architecture teaching pane with glossy symbols

title: Migration decision table
points: Decision grid: server rehost -> Transform MGN; database replication -> DMS; schema change -> SCT/conversion; file/object transfer -> DataSync; managed runtime -> replatform; capability extraction -> refactor.
layout: thin glass architecture teaching pane with glossy symbols

title: Wave readiness and acceptance table
points: Checklist: owners, dependency map, landing zone, connectivity, data protection, test evidence, cutover plan, rollback trigger, monitoring and decommission gate. Remember that validated behavior closes a wave.
layout: thin glass architecture teaching pane with glossy symbols
